chunks: 5688 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who intentionally drank medicine while she was pregnant and did not inform her husband of that, so she miscarried her child. He said: “If it had a bone upon which flesh had grown, then upon her is a diyyah which she gives to its father. And if it was an ʿalaqah or a muḍghah, then upon her is forty dinars or a ghurrah, which she pays to its father.”
So I said to him: “Then she does not inherit her child from his blood money along with his father?” He said: “No, because she killed him, so she does not inherit from him.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ دِينَارًا: forty dinars as a specified monetary compensation
key_terms.دِيَةٌ: blood money or financial compensation due for wrongful killing
key_terms.عَلَقَةً: an embryonic stage described as a clot-like form
key_terms.غُرَّةً: a compensatory slave-payment recognized in legal rulings
key_terms.لَا تَرِثُهُ: she does not inherit from him due to causing his death
key_terms.مُضْغَةً: an embryonic stage described as a chewed lump of flesh

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pregnant woman intentionally causes a miscarriage, and does she inherit from the child’s blood money?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a pregnant woman who intentionally causes the loss of her fetus, specifying financial liability according to the stage of fetal development. It also establishes that because she caused the killing, she does not inherit from the child’s diyyah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5688 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a woman who intentionally drank medicine while she was pregnant without informing her husband, causing her to miscarry his child.
Imam (as) said: "If the fetus had developed bones upon which flesh had grown, she must pay the full diyyah (blood money) to the father. However, if it was a clot of blood (alaqah) or a lump of flesh (mudghah), then she must pay forty dinars or provide a compensatory slave (ghurrah) to the father."

I then asked: "Does she inherit any share of the blood money for her child along with the father?"
Imam (as) replied: "No, because she killed the child, and therefore she does not inherit from it."
